A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FPTQuant with the same authors, core transforms, and optimization framework. All 25 pages of v1 and 28 pages of v2, including appendices, are readable and support matching text, equations, tables, and figures across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantization accuracy, inference benchmarks, and ablations, including Tables 1–2 and Appendices E–H.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds component ablations, reasoning evaluations, perturbation studies, and training-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The default six-transform design and two-stage optimization remain. v2 adds an evaluated FPTQuant+Ph variant incorporating FlatQuant's online query/key transform (Appendix F, Table 12). Reclassifying Tu as an existing transform does not remove it from the method.

E1.justification: v2 adds actual evaluations on MMLU and GSM8K, extending task coverage beyond WikiText-2 and the six retained common-sense tasks (Appendix H, Table 17). MMLU also appears in new ablations. This substantially broadens the capabilities evaluated; Qwen-2.5 7B experiments were already present in v1's appendices.

E2.justification: OSTQuant joins the static and dynamic comparisons. Conversely, QuaRot and FlatQuant are removed specifically from the training-loss comparison (v1 Table 12 versus v2 Table 15), while remaining elsewhere. QuaRot-opt in v2's main table corresponds to the already optimized QuaRot baseline in v1.

E3.justification: v2 adds model configurations including Ministral 8B and Qwen-2.5 32B, GPTQ evaluations, and unquantized parameter-perturbation protocols. Qwen-32B uses 512-token training sequences and method-dependent training lengths. Appendix D specifies 2048-token dynamic evaluation, replacing v1's general 4096-token rule for non-Llama-2 models. The complete main-table W4A8KV4 comparison is replaced by more limited appendix comparisons.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained individual-transform and optimization ablations, v2 adds integrated component ablations (Table 3), activation-outlier visualization (Figure 2), the Ph hybrid study (Table 12), an Lp sensitivity sweep (Table 14), and Gaussian-perturbation tests (Figure 4 and Table 21). Appendix K additionally compares inversion and rotation costs. These investigate component contributions, mechanisms, numerical stability, and computational overhead.

E5.justification: v1 already reports three-seed activation studies and uncertainty for the Tu ablation. v2 substantially extends reporting with three-seed means and standard deviations for a main-result subset and new ablations, five-seed perturbation results, and repeated operation timings. Appendix D newly specifies three-seed medians for FPTQuant and OSTQuant dynamic results; this does not establish an increase from a documented earlier run count.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive reasoning, model, GPTQ, ablation, and timing results and revises retained entries. In Table 2, Llama-2 7B W4A4KV4 perplexity changes from 940 to 603 for FPTQuant and 951 to 106 for FlatQuant, although v2 Table 12 retains the old values. Dynamic Llama-3 8B FPTQuant perplexity changes from 7.17 to 7.67 alongside revised evaluation settings, so this is not a demonstrated same-setting deterioration.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.1 and its Appendix C proof remain unchanged. Limited mathematical revisions include removing Wg from the output-side local-optimization sum (v1 Equation 10 versus v2 Equation 9) and refining block-Hadamard cost from O(n log n) to O(n log(n/K)) in the transform-cost table.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions narrow the novelty claim from four transforms to three. Tu remains implemented but is now associated with prior OSTQuant work. The central accuracy–speed positioning, up-to-3.9× speedup, and comparison with a method up to 29% slower are retained.

C2.justification: v2 adds explicit architectural applicability conditions, explanations connecting residual outliers across blocks, and interpretations of FlatQuant's numerical instability and OSTQuant's failure to preserve function. It also discusses weaker reasoning performance relative to FlatQuant and inconsistent GPTQ benefits. Limitations expand to decoding-benchmark constraints, integer hardware support, and untested MoE and microscaling extensions.

D1.justification: v2 newly discloses frozen/shared teacher weights, per-block gradient checkpointing, OSTQuant reproduction sources, and more detailed timing and inversion procedures. Core calibration and parametrization details remain. Appendix D replaces v1's explicit learning rates with validation-based selection without listing all selected values, reducing specificity in that respect.

R1.justification: v2 integrates OSTQuant into related work, credits its relationship to Tu, and critiques its function-preservation properties. It adds deployment and microscaling references while dropping several QAT citations and QuIP#. These are focused updates to prior-work coverage and attribution; the central expressivity-versus-cost positioning remains.

P1.justification: v2 clarifies quantization and mergeability explanations, folds the standalone Tu subsection into Other transforms, reorganizes experimental setup, and subdivides the compute-resource appendix. It also separates the impact statement and changes citation style. Much of the original prose and the overall introduction–method–experiments–discussion sequence remain.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from single-column to two-column conference layout. Figure 1 is recolored, Table 1 is reorganized, and Table 2 changes its model columns and bit-width blocks. New diagnostic figures and multiple ablation, uncertainty, and timing tables substantially expand the visual presentation; retained figures are also resized and relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation through integrated component ablations, numerical-stability tests, broader model evaluation, and reasoning comparisons with seed-based uncertainty. These address important gaps in v1's evidence, while revised novelty attribution and applicability discussion improve precision. Unreconciled scores between Tables 2 and 12 weaken some comparisons, and reasoning results expose a larger FlatQuant advantage, but the added controlled evidence and clearer limitations provide a substantial net improvement.
